title: Kummer additivity
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ for any $n\geq1$, and the specified pro-etale Tate twist [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. A line bundle means an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Choose $N\geq1$ with $\ell^N A=0$ and put $m=\ell^N$. On $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, let $\delta_{m,T}:H^1(T,\mathbf G_m)\to H^2(T,\mu_m)$ be the connecting homomorphism of the ordinary Kummer short exact sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], with the injective-resolution convention [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor]. Put $L_{m,A,T}=\mu_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A_T$ and $\varphi_{m,A,T}:\mu_m\to L_{m,A,T}$, $z\mapsto z\otimes1_A$ [def-pur-kummer-module-coefficients].

For a line bundle $M$, let $\alpha_T(M)\in H^1(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf G_m)$ be the class of its frame torsor $\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,M)$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor, lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Define
$$c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(M)=H^2(\varphi_{m,A,T})(\delta_{m,T}(\alpha_T(M)))\in H^2(T_{\mathrm{et}},L_{m,A,T}).$$
Interpret this as a morphism $A_T\to L_{m,A,T}[2]$ in the ordinary etale derived category, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Pull this morphism through [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and use the canonical projection-induced identification $\nu_T^*L_{m,A,T}\cong A_T(1)$ supplied by the root-tower reductions [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Denote the result by
$$c_{1,A}(M):A_T\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].$$
This class is independent of the chosen killing exponent $N$. For any two line bundles $M,P$ on $T$,
$$c_{1,A}(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}P)=c_{1,A}(M)+c_{1,A}(P).$$
For every morphism $f:T'\to T$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $f^*c_{1,A}(M)=c_{1,A}(f^*M)$, under the canonical constant-coefficient and Tate-twist comparisons. In particular this equality holds when $f$ is the projection from a base change $T'=T\times_B B'$ with $T'$ in this class. The same additivity and pullback equalities hold for $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}$ under the comparisons [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].

proof.text: The construction is defined for every $n\geq1$: since $\ell$ belongs to the maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)$, $\ell^n A_{E,n}=0$, so a killing exponent exists without requiring the ramification index to divide $n$. The integer $m=\ell^N$ is invertible on $T$, since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Thus the ordinary Kummer sequence is short exact by lem-amb-kummer-any-base. The coefficient morphism $\varphi(z)=z\otimes1_A$ is a homomorphism of abelian sheaves by the tensor relations in def-pur-kummer-module-coefficients. No tensor product of $\mathbf G_m$ with $A$ is used.

By lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor the frame construction applies to arbitrary schemes, and carries tensor product to contracted product. By lem-sc-torsor-h1 contracted product is addition in $H^1$. Hence $\alpha_T(M\otimes P)=\alpha_T(M)+\alpha_T(P)$. More explicitly, on a common trivializing cover, frames $s_i,t_i$ with transitions $g_{ij},h_{ij}$ give frames $s_i\otimes t_i$ with transitions $g_{ij}h_{ij}$; the map from the contracted product of frame torsors sends $[s,t]$ to $s\otimes t$. This checks the sign and product convention without using the curve-only Picard identification.

The categories of constant-coefficient module sheaves, including abelian sheaves at integer coefficients, have enough injectives by lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives. Global sections is additive and left exact because it is evaluation at the final object and kernels of sheaves are computed objectwise. Apply lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor to global sections of abelian etale sheaves and to the Kummer short exact sequence. Its degree-one connecting morphism is a morphism of abelian groups, and its degree-two derived functor is additive. Therefore both $\delta_{m,T}$ and $H^2(\varphi)$ preserve addition. Applying these two homomorphisms to the equality in step 2 gives $c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(M\otimes P)=c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(M)+c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(P)$. By lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget the target abelian cohomology is the cohomology of the underlying $A$-module sheaf. Its identification with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A_T,L_{m,A,T}[2])$ is additive: use lem-pur-rhom-global-sections with first input $A_T$, noting that $\mathcal Hom_A(A_T,I)=I$ by evaluation at $1$ in each degree of an injective resolution. Thus the same equality holds for etale derived morphisms.

proof.text: For $f:T'\to T$, inverse image of the frame torsor followed by extension along $f^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$ is the frame torsor of $f^*M$. To see this, send a pulled-back frame to its pullback as a local basis of $f^*M$; on a trivializing cover both torsors are the units sheaf, with the same transition units $f^*g_{ij}$. The two clauses of lem-sc-etale-torsor-h1-functoriality therefore give $H^1(c_{\mathbf G_m})f^*\alpha_T(M)=\alpha_{T'}(f^*M)$. Pullback of an invertible module is invertible directly from its local rank-one trivializations.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, applied to inverse image and extension of the structure group

proof.text:
Pull the Kummer sequence back to $T'_{\mathrm{et}}$. Its comparison to the Kummer sequence of $T'$ has vertical maps $c_\mu,c_{\mathbf G_m},c_{\mathbf G_m}$: the squares commute because pullback of units commutes with $m$-th powers and inclusion of roots. By lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback (3) and naturality for morphisms of short exact sequences in lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor (1),
$$H^2(c_\mu)f^*\delta_{m,T}=\delta_{m,T'}H^1(c_{\mathbf G_m})f^*.$$
Here inverse image is exact, as required in that pullback theorem. By lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback the roots and tensor twists have the requisite canonical comparisons. They commute with $\varphi$ because both composites send $z$ to $c_\mu(z)\otimes1_A$. Naturality in the coefficient sheaf, part (2) of the site-cohomology-pullback theorem, and step 4 now yield
$$f^*c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(M)=c^{\mathrm{et}}_{1,A}(f^*M).$$ To check that this is also pullback of the derived morphism in step 3, choose injective $A$-module resolutions $L_{m,A,T}\to I^\bullet$ and $f^{-1}L_{m,A,T}\to J^\bullet$, and a comparison $\beta:f^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ over the identity. Module inverse image agrees naturally with abelian inverse image by lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-pullback-forget-naturality, so is exact here. By lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget the underlying abelian sheaves of the terms of these resolutions have zero positive global cohomology. They therefore compute abelian cohomology by lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity (2). Comparing them to abelian injective resolutions computes the same pullback formula of lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback: the two comparison maps into a target injective resolution are homotopic because they lift the same augmentation. A degree-two cocycle $s\in\Gamma(T,I^2)$ represents under lem-pur-rhom-global-sections the chain map $A_T[0]\to I^\bullet[2]$, $1\mapsto s$. Its exact inverse image followed by $\beta[2]$ sends $1$ to $\beta(f^{-1}s)$, precisely the cocycle in that cohomological pullback formula. Hence the equality just proved is the equality of pulled-back etale derived morphisms as well.

proof.text:
Identify the pulled etale twist with the specified pro-etale twist as follows. A primitive $m$-th root $\zeta\in k$ trivializes both etale and pro-etale roots sheaves by $a\mapsto\zeta^a$. Indeed $X^m-1$ splits over $k$ into distinct linear factors, so its roots on any $k$-scheme are locally constant choices among these $m$ roots. By lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact (1), comparison pulls the finite constant coefficient sheaves to the same constants; hence the natural roots comparison is the identity in these coordinates. Tensoring with the finite constant $A$ also gives the identity: a presentation of the finite $\mathbf Z/m$-module $A$ expresses this tensor as a cokernel of maps of finite sums of the roots sheaf, and the exact additive comparison functor of part (2) preserves that presentation. On the pro-etale side, lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free (2),(3) identify the projection from the root tower after tensoring with $A$ with
$$\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell}A_T\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \mu_{m,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A_T,$$
since $mA=0$. This is the same $A_T(1)$ as in def-coefficient-twists-detailed; its inverse defines the canonical identification in the statement. The auxiliary primitive root only checks invertibility, and does not enter the projection-defined map. Applying the additive functor def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback to step 3 proves pro-etale additivity. For pullback, the site inclusions defining $
u$ commute with base change on underlying schemes: both orders send an etale $V	o T$ to $V	imes_TT'$. The composition isomorphism of inverse images in lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition therefore identifies $f^{-1}
u_T^*$ with $
u_{T'}^*f^{-1}$. It is exact on the module complexes here. The projection comparison commutes with $f^{-1}$: in the finite roots and tensor coordinates this is precisely $z\otimes a\mapsto f^*z\otimes a$, and these are the canonical Tate-twist pullback comparisons of det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists. Applying this identification to step 5 proves $f^*c_{1,A}(M)=c_{1,A}(f^*M)$. A base-change projection is such an $f$, so it gives the base-change clause.

proof.text: Finally let $N'\geq N$ and $d=\ell^{N'-N}$. Map the Kummer sequence for $\ell^{N'}$ to that for $\ell^N$ by $z\mapsto z^d$ on the roots and middle units sheaves, and the identity on the last units sheaf. The right square commutes because $(z^d)^{\ell^N}=z^{\ell^{N'}}$. Naturality in lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor gives $H^2((\cdot)^d)\delta_{\ell^{N'},T}=\delta_{\ell^N,T}$. After tensoring with $A$ the power map is the canonical isomorphism of finite etale twists in lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback. Inserting $1_A$ commutes with it. The tower projections in step 6 have exactly these power transitions; hence the etale and pro-etale classes agree for the two exponents. Any pair of killing exponents can be compared to their maximum, proving independence.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $T$ be a
separated finite-type
$k$-scheme. For a line bundle $M$ on $T$ let

$$
c_1(M):\Lambda_T\longrightarrow\Lambda_T(1)[2]
$$

be the class of the $A$-torsor of height $\ell^N$-th roots of a
trivialization of $M$, i.e. the image of the class of $M$ in
$H^1(T_{\Et},\mathbf G_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$ under the connecting
morphism of the Kummer exact sequence of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum] (the identification
$H^1(T_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(T)$ is the standard one:
the $A$-torsor of isomorphisms $\mathcal O_T\to M$ recovers $M$
as $(T\times M)/\mathbf G_m$).
Then

$$
c_1(M\otimes N)=c_1(M)+c_1(N),
$$

and $c_1$ is compatible with pullback and with base change.

proof.text:
The boundary used here is the Kummer boundary of [def-pur-affine-line-datum], with its cohomology interpreted as in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].
The connecting morphism of the Kummer exact sequence is a morphism of
$\Lambda$-modules on the group structure defined by the torsor
product, which corresponds under the identification
$H^1(T,\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(T)$ to the tensor product of
line bundles; it therefore satisfies $c_1(M\otimes N)=c_1(M)+c_1(N)$. Functoriality is the functoriality of the
connecting morphism of the exact sequence and of the torsor
identification.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q87-9b3415c8c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item JSON, the current blueprint statement and proof, the unit sk-prop-a1-kummer and the cited Kummer unit, every cited node statement (none missing or merged), the three citers, and Stacks 03PL and 040E. The statement correction (E7) is justified. By 03PL the m-th power map is etale-surjective, so G_m tensor A = 0 when mA=0, and the blueprint's H^1(G_m tensor A) class would vanish; O(1) on P^1 shows the class must be nonzero. The repair is the standard class: the frame torsor in H^1(G_m), the Kummer boundary into H^2(mu_m), insertion z -> z tensor 1, then nu^* with the projection identification to A_T(1). It holds for every n >= 1 (N=n kills A, and the e|n condition of def-pur-affine-line-datum is not imported). It keeps the type Lambda_T -> Lambda_T(1)[2] with Lambda=A, keeps additivity, pullback and base change, and adds exponent independence, which is proved. Steps checked: (1) exponent and Kummer exactness; (2) the contracted product of frame torsors, with the sign checked; (3) horseshoe additivity and H^2 = Hom_D(A_T, L[2]) via rhom-global-sections and module/abelian forget; (4) both clauses of torsor H^1 functoriality, no flatness needed; (5) the composite of site pullback (3) and horseshoe (1) gives f^* delta_T = delta_T' f^*, plus the passage to derived morphisms; (6) nu^{-1} mu = mu in the coordinates of a primitive root, tensor with A via a finite presentation, twist-sheaf-locally-free (2),(3), commutation of f^{-1} with nu^* via site composition, and the cartesian twists; (7) the power-map diagram of Kummer sequences, whose right square commutes because (z^d)^{l^N} = z^{l^N'}. No cycle, no new nodes, no SGA, route unchanged. All 16 declared tool uses are accepted as generic tools; lem-amb-kummer-any-base is needed because the unit's own route node covers only curves. Note for later: the unsplit citer lem-pur-divisor-class cites this item for the degree-one kappa additivity, which neither the old nor the new statement asserts; that should be fixed when that citer is split.
